families.theme: Burbot and under-ice locksmiths: a smooth eel-bodied fish grows its single chin barbel into a key-bit organ and opens paired shutter-like fin folds to slip through sealed winter channels. The key is living anatomy, not a carried object.
evolution_design: Small smooth long burbot with a broad flat head, one thick curved chin barbel ending in one broad key-tooth, a short soft dorsal fold and a rounded tail. A watchful curious face and large white eye. Full fish, no arms or feet.

Longer heavier eel-bodied burbot curves in one loose C; the SINGLE chin barbel thickens into a blunt two-bit key-shaped organ. Two broad soft pleated dorsal/anal fin folds open like paired curved shutters along the body. Long rounded tail, large expressive fish face; no metal key, lock prop, clothing, machinery or tiny details.
families.habitat: Cold lake floors and winter under-ice channels, inspired by Minnesota burbot ecology.

sources.title: Minnesota DNR: Burbot (Eelpout)

sources.title: Minnesota DNR: Burbot species profile
sources.supports: Bottom-oriented fish active during low light in winter; midwinter spawning before ice-out.
sources.fantasy_extension: Under-ice locksmith role is original, not a claim about real fish.
